contextual.summary: York automatically checks UCAS applications from Home-fee students at UK state schools and may make an offer up to two grades lower if your postcode (or refugee/humanitarian protection status, care experience or estrangement) qualifies; completing a York access programme can mean up to three grades lower.
contextual.typicalReduction: Up to two grades below the standard offer (up to three grades below after completing Next Step York, Black Access or Realising Opportunities)

criteria.detail: Must have attended a UK state-funded school, college or sixth form and pay UK (Home) fees — required for every contextual route
Home postcode is eligible under York's postcode data (a postcode checker for 2027 entry is on the page; the measure used is not named)
Experience of being in local authority care — tell York via the Additional Information Form (deadline Friday 28 May 2027)
Estranged from your family — tell York via the Additional Information Form

contextual.rulesText: If you meet the criteria for one of York's contextual-admissions routes (plus any subject requirements), you may get a lower offer. For every route you must have attended a UK state-funded school, college or sixth form and pay Home fees. Postcode eligibility is assessed automatically from UCAS; care-experienced and estranged applicants use the Additional Information Form.

programmes.name: Next Step York
programmes.summary: Two-year access programme for Year 12 students in England, mixing online and on-campus events, a July summer residential and support with choosing and applying to university.
programmes.whoCanApply: Year 12 students at English state schools or colleges (state school from Year 7 to 11), living in the UK for at least three years, with the potential to get BCC or above, who meet at least one of the widening-participation criteria.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Essential: potential to achieve BCC+ at A-level (or equivalent); in your first year of post-16 study at an English state school, sixth form or college; attended a state school from Year 7 to Year 11; UK resident for the last three years. Plus at least one of: Black or South Asian background; Gypsy, Roma, Traveller, Showmen or Boater background; care experience; estranged; seeking asylum or refugee status; free school meals or discretionary payments; disability or long-term health condition; military/service family; parents didn't go to university (or went as mature students during your secondary education); young carer; living in a priority neighbourhood (postcode checker on the page).
benefits: Alternative Widening Participation offer up to three grades below the standard offer (conditional on completing the YorJourney module; e.g. Economics BBC instead of AAB)
Could be considered for a guaranteed interview or offer at York
programmes.offerReduction: Up to three grades below the standard offer

runs.text: Starts January 2027 with an online launch; events January–July 2027 (including a July summer residential), then Year 2 support through Year 13

notes: All course pages are for 2027/28 entry; no 2028-entry pages were published when checked (2026-10-17).
No admissions test (such as the TMUA) is listed for any of these courses.

Many York courses give an alternative offer up to one A-level grade lower for a good EPQ grade (the grade needed varies by course), and some for Core Maths or completing a free York online course (MOOC).

York gives an alternative Widening Participation offer (up to three grades below the standard offer) to students who complete Realising Opportunities, as well as its own Next Step York and Black Access programmes.

Economics department page: 'There are opportunities for you to spend time abroad during your course. You'll also have the chance to take a placement year.' York also lists a four-year 'Economics with a year abroad' route.
York's main undergraduate open days take place in June and July (post-16 outreach page).
York offers a guaranteed offer (or interview) to applicants living in Yorkshire, the Humber or Tees Valley who are on course to meet the entry requirements.

Other relevant York courses not recorded here: Business and Management (BA/BSc), Economics and Mathematics (AAA including Maths), Economics and Philosophy, Economics, Econometrics and Finance, History/Economics and BA PPE.
